info.name: AI Voice Agent - Dashboard API
info.description:
# AI Voice Agent - Dashboard API

Import this collection, then run **1. Auth -> Login** first. It stores the
access token in a collection variable, and every other request picks it up automatically.

## Two ways to authenticate

| Who | How |
|---|---|
| A person | `Authorization: Bearer <token>` from Login. Set once for the whole collection. |
| The AI voice agent | `X-API-Key: {{apiKey}}`. Set on the requests in *6. AI agent*. |

## Variables

- `baseUrl` - http://localhost:8080
- `apiKey` - the agent key from application.yml
- `token`, `leadId`, `callLogId` - captured automatically as you work through the folders

## Suggested order

1. Login
2. Leads -> Create a fresh lead
3. Call queue -> Take work to call
4. Calls -> Report what happened
5. Dashboard -> any range

The whole API is **camelCase**, in bodies and in query parameters.

## How dialling actually works (no background scheduler)

Nothing runs on a timer. The AI agent pulls work by calling
`POST /api/v1/call-queue/claims` whenever it is ready for another lead - that single call
covers fresh leads AND due callbacks, since a booked callback becomes claimable again the
moment its time arrives. Report the result with
`POST /api/v1/calls/{callLogId}/outcome` and the lead moves itself: retry, callback, or closed.

If a worker crashes between claim and outcome, that lead is stuck in *dialing* until someone
calls `POST /api/v1/call-queue/recoveries` - see *Call queue*.

item.name: 1. Login and accounts
item.description: Get a token first - everything else depends on it.

request.description: Stores the access token in the {{token}} collection variable.
Confirms the token still works.
Admins only. Retries, the wait after each kind of failed call, and the hours calls are allowed.
Admins only. Roles: orgAdmin, manager, agent, viewer.
Public endpoint. Only useful on a fresh database.

item.name: 2. API key for the AI agent
item.description: The key the voice-agent application authenticates with. Admin only.

request.description: Returns the prefix only. The key itself is stored hashed and cannot be read back.

exec: console.log("New API key saved to {{apiKey}}:", b.apiKey);

request.description: Returns the full key ONCE and saves it into {{apiKey}}. The previous key stops working immediately.
The agent loses access at once.

item.name: 3. Leads
item.description: The people to call. A fresh lead needs only a name and a phone number.

request.description: All it takes is a name and a number. Saved with pipelineStatus "new" and queued for a call straight away. Stores the id in {{leadId}}.

body.raw:
{
  "name": "The Dev",
  "phone": "+919000000102",
  "project": "My Home Sanctuary",
  "actionType": "siteVisit",
  "scheduledFor": "2026-09-05T10:00:00+05:30",
  "reminderEnabled": true,
  "notes": "Lead confirmed the site-visit date and time."
}

request.description: The action fields are accepted here too, for importing. Each actionType requires its own time.
The same number as the lead you just created, only formatted differently. Spaces and dashes are ignored, so this is rejected.
Safe to call repeatedly - this is what the agent should use.

exec: pm.test("the field you sent was applied", () => pm.expect(b.pipelineStatus).to.eql("queued"));
pm.test("notes was applied", () => pm.expect(b.notes).to.eql("Reviewed by the sales desk."));

request.description: Partial update: only the fields you send change. name, phone, project, id all stay exactly as they were.
Full replace: send the whole lead. Any field you leave out is cleared, unlike PATCH. Use this when you have the complete record; use PATCH when you only want to change a few fields.

item.name: Requeue a lead

request.description: Run before the do-not-call request below - a suppressed lead refuses to be re-queued (422) until the flag is cleared.

item.description: Use PATCH /api/v1/leads/{leadId} with pipelineStatus=queued instead of a dedicated queue endpoint.

request.description: Stops all future calls immediately. This is a terminal demo step - nothing after it re-queues this lead.
Managers and admins only - the AI agent's API key gets 403 here on purpose. Uses the collection Bearer token, not X-API-Key.
Confirms the delete actually took effect.

item.name: 4. Calls and history
item.description: Take work, place the call, report what happened. The outcome is what moves the lead.

exec: console.log("Nothing due right now - create a lead first.");

request.description: Atomically claims due leads, so two callers never get the same person. Saves the first attempt into {{callLogId}}.

exec: const b = pm.response.json(); if (b.callLogId) pm.collectionVariables.set("callLogId", b.callLogId);

request.description: Ignores the schedule. Repeating the same idempotencyKey returns the attempt already open instead of a second one.
Schedules a retry with backoff, moved inside calling hours.

body.raw:
{
  "outcome": "answered",
  "disposition": "siteVisitBooked",
  "talkSeconds": 214,
  "siteVisitAt": "2026-09-06T11:00:00+05:30",
  "summary": "Wants the 3 BHK, visiting Saturday.",
  "recordingUrl": "https://recordings.local/call-abc.mp3",
  "leadName": "Shrikant Giri",
  "leadProject": "My Home Sanctuary",
  "leadQuery": "Can 2 BHK and 3 BHK be combined to make 5 BHK?"
}

request.description: leadName / leadProject / leadQuery write back what the call taught us, so the lead record fills itself in.
Booked at their time, and it does NOT use up a retry attempt.

item.name: Move a call to a time they asked for

request.description: 23:30 is outside calling hours, so it lands at 09:00 the next morning.
Every attempt ever made for this lead, newest first. Read from the call log, not the lead.

item.name: 5. Dashboard
item.description:
Every number in one request, over the period you choose.

- **Current status** - the tiles, the pipeline and final-status breakdowns, the action split -
  is read from the **lead** records, because only the lead knows where things stand now.
- **History** - calls, pick-up rate, talk time, outcomes, dispositions, the daily trend -
  is read from the **call log**, because only the log knows what actually happened.

The same window applies to both: leads are counted by when they arrived, calls by when they
were placed, so the tiles and the charts always describe the same period.

request.description: Since midnight, in the company timezone.
The last 7 days.
The last 15 days.
The last 30 days. This is the default when range is omitted.
The last 90 days.
Everything ever recorded.

exec: console.log("Window:", b.window.range, b.window.from, "->", b.window.to, "(" + b.window.days + " days)");
console.log("Leads:", b.totals.totalLeads, "| pending:", b.totals.pending, "| converted:", b.totals.converted);

request.description: from is required; to defaults to now.

item.name: 6. AI agent (API key)
item.description: The voice-agent application sends X-API-Key instead of logging in. No token, no expiry.

item.name: Agent pushes in a fresh lead

exec: const b = pm.response.json(); if (b.length) pm.collectionVariables.set("callLogId", b[0].callLogId);
